specification.problem: Exact synthesis of single-qubit unitaries over the Clifford-cyclotomic gate set (Clifford group plus z-rotation by pi/n, n positive even), minimizing the number of pi/n z-rotations; specialized here to the Clifford+T case n=4 as a tiny instance.
specification.reconstruction_scope: Only the ring characterization of candidate exactly synthesizable unitaries and the generic T-count-reducing step structure for n=4 (Clifford+T). The paper's general-n algorithm, its minimality proof, and the proof that the ring characterization fails for 100% of even n are outside scope and not reconstructed.

symbols.meaning: even positive integer defining the rotation angle pi/n
number of pi/n z-rotations (T-count for n=4)

equations.label: Ring of entries
equations.description: Ring whose unitaries were shown to coincide with exactly synthesizable ones for n=4.
equations.abstract_quote: the group of unitaries with entries over the ring $\mathbb{Z}[e^{i\frac{\pi}{n}},1/2]$
equations.justification: Ring is named in the abstract.

equations.label: Gate set
equations.description: Clifford-cyclotomic gate set generated by the Clifford group and the pi/n z-rotation.
equations.abstract_quote: the Clifford group plus a $z$-rotation by $\frac{\pi}{n}$
equations.justification: Direct description of the gate set; the generated-group notation is mine.
assumptions: Gates are considered up to global phase conventions not specified in the abstract.

equations.label: Exact synthesis form
equations.description: Decomposition with k pi/n rotations interleaved with Cliffords, k minimal.
equations.abstract_quote: outputs a decomposition using the minimum number of $\frac{\pi}{n}$ $z$-rotations
equations.justification: Inferred from the minimality claim; the exact decomposition form is a generic assumption.
assumptions: Product ordering convention is a choice.

equations.label: Characterization for n=4
equations.latex: \{U\in U(2): U\ \text{exactly synthesizable over Clifford+T}\}=U(2)\cap M_2(R_4)
equations.description: For n=4 exactly synthesizable unitaries equal unitaries with entries in R_4; equality up to global phase conventions is not specified.
equations.abstract_quote: the group of exactly synthesizable unitaries was shown to be equal to the group of unitaries with entries over the ring
equations.justification: Stated for n=4 in the abstract.
assumptions: Phase normalization as in the original Clifford+T result.

equations.label: Unitarity constraint
equations.description: Unitarity condition on matrices with ring entries.
equations.justification: Standard definition of unitary with entries in a ring closed under needed conjugation.
assumptions: R_n is closed under complex conjugation.

registers.name: q
registers.role: single qubit acted on by U

steps.description: Given U with entries in R_n, check unitarity.

Iteratively multiply by Clifford and R_z(pi/n) gates to reduce a ring-based complexity measure (for n=4, the denominator exponent), until a Clifford remains; the reduction rule for general n is not given in the abstract.
For n=4, the exactly synthesizable set equals unitaries over R_4.

specification.classical_postprocessing: Classical algorithm outputs the gate sequence; its details are not given in the abstract.

Decomposition form in eq_3 is generic, not the paper's.
